title: The underwater event profiler: An event‐based vision sensor approach for quantifying marine‐snow size distributions
content:
Abstract

We present an underwater particle imaging system based on an event-based vision sensor (EVS), the underwater event profiler (UEP), together with an event-processing pipeline, evsMarineSnow, and demonstrate their application to quantify marine-particle size distributions (PSDs) from high-temporal-resolution event-based observations. The UEP–evsMarineSnow framework reconstructs particle trajectories and estimates particle size and particle residence time to derive number-size distributions, number-density PSDs, and volume-concentration PSDs. Tracking, residence-time reconstruction, and size-estimation performance of evsMarineSnow were assessed using synthetic event datasets spanning a range of particle sizes and velocities. Valid-track rates exceeded 90% across most tested conditions, and particle-size estimates for simulated particles ≥ 0.5 mm exhibited biases generally below 4%. Field deployments of moored UEP systems at 45 and 85 m depth successfully recorded particle passages as event datasets under natural marine conditions, generating on the order of 104 particle tracks per 10-s observation. The resulting UEP-derived number densities were comparable to previously reported coastal values. To evaluate the influence of temporal sampling, pseudo-frame datasets were generated from identical EVS observations across frame rates from 0.1 to 100 fps. Apparent frame-rate effects primarily reflected differences in sampling effort, with low sampling effort disproportionately affecting sparsely populated large-particle classes and volume-concentration estimates. Together, these assessments demonstrate the proof of concept for deriving marine-particle PSDs from high-temporal-resolution event-based observations and highlight the potential advantage of EVS for increasing sampling effort, particularly for sparsely occurring large particles.
